podcast.body: Released in 1978, this song is widely considered the last great quality hit of disco music. Its release marked the professional beginning of disco's decline, as the genre subsequently began to devolve into parody, becoming somewhat scatological, parodic, and at times ridiculous. "profesionalmente se considera que el principio del final de la música disco es en 1978 cuando Gloria Gaynor publica el I will Survive, que está considerado el último gran hit de calidad de la música disco."

podcast.body: Released in 1978, this song reached number one on the Billboard Hot 100 and became an anthem for the gay community. In 2016, the Library of Congress selected its original recording for preservation in the National Recording Registry due to its cultural, historical, and artistic significance. "In 2016, the Library of Congress deemed her original recording to be culturally, historically and artistically significant and selected it for preservation in the national recording registry."

This "glorious breakup disco song" became a dance hit, an anthem for female empowerment, and was widely embraced by gay culture. Despite its eventual fame, it was originally released as a B-side in 1978, with the A-side being a cover of the Righteous Brothers' "Substitute," which failed. DJs, however, discovered "I Will Survive" and began playing it in clubs, launching its success. "What people forget is that I Will Survive was a B side."
